newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Escudo falls sharply vs mark on French news.
newsitem.headline: Escudo falls sharply vs mark on French news.

text.p: The Portuguese escudo dropped sharply against the mark, following the lead of other southern European currencies, after France's leftwing government said it wanted further discussions on the European Union's Stability Pact.

The currency was down at 101.47/50 to the mark after opening at 101.13/18. "After the news from the Ecofin (European finance ministers meeting), the black clouds hanging over the single currency have instensified," said one trader.
"I would not be surprised to see the Bank of Portugal entering the market to buy escudos to prevent a greater fall," added another.

The new Socialist-led government in Paris has called for a "period of consultation" on the Stability Pact which sets down a system of future budget limits for countries that join a single European currency, with fines for those that break them.

The Stability Pact is seen by Germany in particular as vital to ensure that members of the planned single currency do not waiver in their commitment to sound budgetary policies after the launch of the euro in January 1999.
